items.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023
items.q: Jason — Colonel Fettig, who just retired by the way — invited me to do the Fiftieth Anniversary of Wolf Trap.

ctx.x: He said, “Fred having played with Harry James when Sonny Payne was playing the drums expected no less from me. I had to step-up my intensity and kick the band with the forcefulness of a Howitzer cannon.

Yeah. I’m famous for drummers. Well that’s what I’ve been told. When I was a guest soloist — one of the most important jobs I’ve ever done in my life — a guest soloist for the President’s own Marine Band, which was very important to me. And Jason — Colonel Fettig, who just retired by the way — invited me to do the Fiftieth Anniversary of Wolf Trap. And so I go in for the rehearsal in Washington and of course here’s the greatest musicians in the world sitting in this band. I said I’ve never seen so many…
It seems like a hard thing to define, like does it have a lot to do with the drummer — where he plays his fills and setting up the downbeat? And you two have to be like in sync.
